title: Morphometry of Ophiothrix (Echinodermata: Ophiuroidea)
author: Renata Alitto
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tz5ep86

steps.title: Measure specimen morphometry
steps.instruction: Measure the specified morphological characters of the specimens using the appropriate tool based on disc diameter.

substeps.instruction: Use an ocular micrometer and AxioVision VS program 40.4.8.20 (Carl Zeiss Microscopy, Germany) attached to a ZEISS Discovery V20 stereomicroscope for specimens with a disc diameter less than 10 mm.
Use a digital Mitutoyo CD-6 CS caliper for specimens with a disc diameter of 10 mm or larger.

Record the following measurements: Disc diameter, Radial shield length, Radial shield width, Disc spine, Arm spine, Second arm spine, Oral diameter, Oral shield length, Oral shield width, Adoral shield length, Adoral shield width, Dorsal arm plate length, Dorsal arm plate width, 1st ventral arm plate length, 1st Ventral arm plate width, 2nd ventral arm plate length, and 2nd ventral arm plate width.

steps.title: Perform multivariate analysis of variance
steps.instruction: Conduct a permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA) to test if morphological characters and dispersion differ between CS.

substeps.instruction: Use the adonis function (package vegan) for PERMANOVA.
Use betadisper and permutest functions (package vegan) to test homogeneity of group dispersions.

steps.title: Execute linear discriminant analysis (LDA)
steps.instruction: Apply LDA using the R environment to distinguish the four Ophiothrix CS and assess classification rates.

substeps.instruction: Construct a correlation matrix to identify multicollinearity; remove variables with a correlation threshold value of 0.9.
Use the lda function (package MASS) to distinguish the four Ophiothrix CS and assess the classification rate of each CS.
Use the predict function (package STATS) and table function (package BASE) to assess classification based on linear discriminants and verify model error.
Visualize results using the ggplot2 package.
Predict Ophiothrix angulata specimens from the type locality (USNM) using the model to verify their related CS.
